components.name: GPU Die
components.reasoning: The GPU die is the primary logic chip that performs rendering and other graphics computations. It is a complex semiconducting chip specifically fabricated for high-performance visual processing tasks, making it essential and reliably procured as a separate unit.

components.name: High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Stack
components.reasoning: HBM stacks are specialized memory modules providing rapid access to large datasets required in GPU operations. They are typically procured separately due to their high bandwidth and low latency, which differentiate them from general-purpose RAM.

components.name: Power Delivery PCB (Printed Circuit Board)
components.reasoning: The power delivery PCB manages the distribution of power across the GPU components, ensuring stable voltage levels for optimal performance under varying loads. It is a distinct assembly that connects major subassemblies and supports secondary power supply integration.

components.name: Heat Sink Module
components.reasoning: A heat sink or thermal solution is critical to dissipate the high temperatures generated by GPU operations. While some GPUs integrate the cooling into the package, it remains a distinct assembly in many designs due to its significant role in reliability and performance optimization.

components.name: Interface Connectors (PCIe/GPU)
components.reasoning: These connectors enable communication between the GPU and other system components, such as the motherboard via PCIe slots or direct connections with displays via HDMI/DVI/DisplayPort interfaces. They are typically separate modules to ensure robustness and flexibility in design.

components.name: VRM (Voltage Regulator Module) Assembly
components.reasoning: VRMs convert power from the power supply unit into stable voltages for GPU components, requiring precise control over current consumption and voltage levels. They are critical subassemblies that provide essential regulation, making them separate items in most GPU designs.

components.name: Memory Controller IC (Memory Subsystem)
components.reasoning: The memory controller manages the data transfer between main memory and the GPUs, playing a key role in overall performance. While some advanced GPUs integrate these functions onto the die, it remains a critical component when separated for procurement or design flexibility.

components.name: On-Board Debug Interface (JTAG/SPI)
components.reasoning: This interface is used for debugging and firmware updates during development and maintenance phases. Though not crucial in all production units, its presence indicates distinct functionality often handled separately from other components.

components.name: Display Interface Connectors (HDMI/DisplayPort/DVI)
components.reasoning: Display interface connectors provide the necessary signals for driving connected monitors or displays directly from the GPU. Their separate procurement allows flexibility in configuration and support diverse display types without redesigning the entire chip.

components.name: Logic Subassembly (Control Circuits/Peripheral Interface Chips)
components.reasoning: This subassembly includes peripheral interface chips for handling signals to peripheral devices, including I/O controllers and other control logic. It is a critical component ensuring seamless interaction between the GPU and system peripherals.
